title_en: Fall 2026 Master's/Doctoral Seminar Auditing: New Students and Integrated-Program Doctoral Entrants
summary: Graduate students starting their module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar in Fall 2026, including Fall 2026 new graduate students and integrated master's-doctoral program students entering the doctoral stage, must apply to audit the seminar offered by their own (advisor's) module. Apply by email to the teaching assistant of the course listed in Attachment 2 by Wednesday, 12 August 2026. Do not formally register for the course during the course registration period.
applies_to: Graduate students taking the first semester of their module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar in Fall 2026: Fall 2026 new graduate students (후기 신입생), and integrated master's-doctoral program students entering the doctoral stage (doctoral seminar audit in the 4th semester). The seminar is a mandatory requirement for completing the master's and doctoral programs, and the first semester must be taken as auditing. Fall 2026 new graduate students must read Attachment 1.

dates.what: Deadline to apply by email to audit the Master's/Doctoral Seminar
English presentation skills seminar, online via Zoom (optional for auditing students; details to be announced later)

conditions: The module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar is a mandatory requirement for completing the master's and doctoral programs and must be taken before completion.

The seminar runs over two semesters: the first semester is auditing only, without course registration; in the second semester you register for the course and give a presentation in English to earn 3 credits.

Integrated master's-doctoral program students must complete both the Master's Seminar (audit in the 1st semester, register and present in the 2nd) and the Doctoral Seminar (audit in the 4th semester, register and present in the 5th), based on entering the doctoral stage in the 4th semester.
Do not formally register for the seminar during the course registration period in your first (auditing) semester.
You must apply to audit the course offered by your own module (your advisor's module), as listed in Attachment 2.
Courses with the same name other than the 16 courses listed in Attachment 2 are not the required seminar; they count only as general graduate courses (their subtitle code and subtitle name differ).
The English presentation skills seminar is not mandatory for auditing students; only those who wish may apply, and attendance is recommended in the semester you register for credit.
steps: Fall 2026 new graduate students: read Attachment 1 (Fall 2026 required Master's/Doctoral Seminar auditing guide for new students) carefully. Note: the attachment content was not included in the notice text and has not been read.

Check Attachment 2 to find the seminar course offered by your own (advisor's) module and the email address of its teaching assistant. Note: the attachment content was not included in the notice text and has not been read.
By Wednesday, 12 August 2026, email the teaching assistant of that course with your student ID number, name, advisor, email address and mobile phone number.
During the course registration period, do not formally register for the seminar course in your auditing semester.
Optional: if you wish, apply for the English presentation skills seminar (Friday, 4 September 2026, 2:00–3:00 p.m., online via Zoom); details will be announced in a later notice.
For questions, contact the department office (Building 301, Room 319); contact details are in the original notice.
translation:
Fall 2026 Graduate Module-Based Master's/Doctoral Seminar [석박세미나] Course Auditing [청강] Guide (New Students / Integrated-Program Students Entering the Doctoral Stage)

This notice explains how to apply to audit [청강] the module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar [석박세미나] courses for the Fall 2026 semester.

Fall 2026 new graduate students [후기 신입생] must check the contents of [Attachment 1] so that there are no mistakes in their auditing application.

1. Overview of the graduate module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar
- It is a required condition for completing the master's and doctoral programs. Master's and doctoral seminars for each module are offered every semester, and you must take the seminar of your own module before completion.
- It runs over two semesters. The first semester is conducted as auditing [청강] without course registration [수강신청], and in the second semester you earn 3 credits through course registration and an English presentation.
- Integrated master's-doctoral program students must complete both the Master's Seminar and the Doctoral Seminar (based on entering the doctoral stage in the 4th semester).
  · Master's Seminar: audit in the 1st semester → register and present in the 2nd semester (3 credits)
  · Doctoral Seminar: audit in the 4th semester → register and present in the 5th semester (3 credits)
  ※ In the first semester (1st semester, 4th semester), you do not formally register for the course; it is conducted as auditing only.

2. Auditing application
- Deadline: by Wednesday, 12 August 2026 [2026. 8. 12.(수)까지]
- How to apply: by email to the teaching assistant in charge of the course you wish to take (see [Attachment 2])
- Information to submit: student ID number / name / advisor / email address / mobile phone number

3. English presentation skills seminar (details to be announced later)
- Date, time and place: Friday, 4 September 2026, 2:00–3:00 p.m., planned to be held online (Zoom)
- Content: a lecture on English presentation skills.
- Note: attendance is not mandatory for auditing students; only those who wish may apply (attendance is recommended in the semester you register for the course).

4. Important notes
a. Courses with the same name other than the 16 courses listed in [Attachment 2] are not the required Master's/Doctoral Seminar; they are recognised as general graduate courses (their subtitle code / subtitle name differ).
b. Because the module-based Master's/Doctoral Seminar is conducted as auditing in the first semester, take care not to formally register for the course during the course registration period.
c. You must apply to audit the course offered by the module you belong to (your advisor's module) (see [Attachment 2]).

5. Inquiries: department office [학부사무실], Building 301, Room 319 (contact details are in the original notice).
